checks_actual_results: The current JDK 21 JAR and frontend dist produced release 0.1.0-s19.2-dev6: manifest v2, Flyway V23, SHA-256 for the JAR and every frontend file, non-secret examples, SQL scripts, operations scripts and five independent guides. The ZIP SHA-256 and packaged Markdown links were checked.

An isolated database preflight read version 0. The first installation migrated to V23 and then failed closed because the required default-admin deployment key was absent; runtime/last-deployment.json required recovery and the service stopped. The missing configuration was added to examples and instructions, a unique key was supplied outside the repository, and the same database was brought up by the forward-fix path without deleting data.

Release dev6 then deployed as a same-schema update using the native MySQL client. Backend readiness passed; an Nginx reverse proxy served packaged frontend assets and API. Edge logged in as the initial administrator, created one system, and re-entered that system after an explicit stop/start and after the update.

For dev6, backup.ps1 created a transactional SQL dump, file archive, configuration snapshot and secret-reference-only plan. All four recorded sizes and hashes matched. restore-drill.ps1 imported into a new database and extracted files. Source and restored schemas each had 191 total tables, Flyway V23 and the same created system; a file marker SHA-256 matched. The marker proves file archive mechanics, not historical business PDF recovery.

All 10 deployment PowerShell scripts parsed; the package browser script parsed. A changed frontend index was rejected by the new SHA-256 guard, and a schema v1 manifest retained the legacy restart path. workspace-validate and targeted whitespace checks passed. The unchanged backend and frontend candidates had already passed the S19.1 package/build and 172/172 frontend tests.
permission_or_failure_result: Missing bootstrap key prevented first-run administrator creation after Flyway V23; the deployment remained stopped with explicit recovery evidence. Tampered frontend bytes failed manifest validation. No secrets were written into the package or verification receipt.
control_limit: The independent package test used a local Nginx container and isolated MySQL schemas. Its recovered file was an explicit marker, not a linked business PDF. Production environment credentials, external identity providers and full functional acceptance were not asserted.
